gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the QNAP TS-464 (Celeron N5095) and the Asustor Lockerstor 4 Gen2 (Celeron N5105) use Jasper Lake chips. Jellyfin's docs say those chips have no AV1 hardware decoding and are 'losing support for QSV on Linux'. The UGREEN DXP4800 Plus's Pentium Gold 8505 is Alder Lake (12th-gen UHD), which falls in Jellyfin's 'Tiger Lake and newer' group for AV1 decoding.
standout_why: I compared against StarryHope 'Synology Alternatives' (cited), StarryHope 'Best 4-Bay NAS' (cited) and our current Dealectric page. All three cover the same point: the DS925+ has no iGPU and Intel boxes have Quick Sync. StarryHope Alternatives says only that the TS-464 is 'a 2021 chip … a generation behind'. None of the three names AV1. None says Jasper Lake (N5095/N5105) can't hardware-decode AV1, and none mentions Jasper Lake QSV support being phased out on Linux. Our page lists the TS-464 and Nimbustor N5105 with just 'UHD'. I couldn't load thisping.com, which ChatGPT cited, because of a TLS certificate error, so I don't know what it says.
decides: For a home user who plans to run Plex or Jellyfin, this backs the DXP4800 Plus (Alder Lake) over ChatGPT's #2 pick, the QNAP TS-464, and its #4 pick, the Asustor Lockerstor 4 Gen2/Gen2+. Both of those use Jasper Lake: they can't hardware-decode AV1 files, and Jellyfin says Jasper Lake QSV 'may stop working in a few years'. This applies to Plex/Jellyfin use only. It does not change the pick for a buyer who only stores files and photos. One side note on 'stay with Synology for photos': in Synology's own words, DSM 7.2.2 'offload[s] media processing to clients and mobile devices'.

findings.value: 'Decoding AV1 8/10-bit - Gen 12 Tiger Lake (11th Gen Core) and newer'
findings.source_title: Jellyfin docs: Intel GPU hardware acceleration
findings.note: This is the project's own documentation.

findings.label: Jasper Lake: no AV1 and QSV being phased out (Jellyfin docs)
findings.value: 'Jasper Lake and Elkhart Lake processors are 10th Gen Pentium/Celeron/Atom, which don't have AV1 acceleration'. Also: 'JSL (Jasper Lake) / EHL (Elkhart Lake) and older generations are losing support for QSV on Linux' and 'may stop working in a few years, by which point you will have to switch to VA-API'. And: 'Gen 11 JSL/EHL graphics - Only support LP encoding mode.'
findings.source_title: Jellyfin docs: Intel GPU hardware acceleration
findings.note: QTS, ADM and UGOS are all Linux-based, so the Linux note applies to these NAS boxes.

findings.label: Intel media-driver platform grouping
findings.value: Intel's media-driver README lists AV1 decode/encode rows for newer platforms through TGLx and up, and has a separate EHL/JSL column. It defines TGLx as 'TGL: Tiger Lake, RKL: Rocket Lake, ADL-S/P/N: Alder Lake, RPL-S/P: Raptor Lake'.
findings.note: The fetched markdown table lost its cell alignment, so I couldn't map each AV1 cell to a column with confidence. I'm using this only for the grouping that puts Alder Lake in the Tiger Lake class. The AV1 claim rests on Jellyfin's wording above.
